issues.description: The return type of Farm.singFarmSong() differs between the specification/template and the solution. The UML and the template declare/expect singFarmSong() to be void and to print the song, while the solution implements singFarmSong() to return a String containing the song text. This mismatch can confuse students about whether they should print the song or return it, and may cause incompatibilities with tests or the provided template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution implementation to match the UML/template by making singFarmSong() a void method that prints each verse (and, if needed, keep a private helper that builds Strings but prints them), or (B) Update the UML and template to specify singFarmSong(): String (and adjust the template signature and problem text to indicate the song is returned rather than printed). Prefer option A to preserve the original UML and printing-based instructions.

issues.description: The Farm song methods are represented with different APIs across artifacts: the problem statement UML and the template Farm.java define singFarmSong() and singFarmSongVerse(Animal) as void methods that print the song, but the solution implementation changes these to return String (singFarmSong():String and singFarmSongVerse(Animal):String). This mismatch in the expected method return behavior creates confusion for students about whether they should print the song or return it as a String, and which signature the tests will expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution methods to match the UML/template and have singFarmSong() and singFarmSongVerse(Animal) be void and perform printing directly; or (B) update the problem statement UML and the template to specify that these methods return String (and adjust template implementation accordingly). Ensure tests and instructions reflect the chosen signature.
